title: Dashboard Studio — traffic to cost decomposition
transcript_summary: AE + SE walked HelioWorks through the new Dashboard Studio: per-path usage lenses, traffic-to-cost decomposition, anomaly detection hooks, and a sandbox demo showing cost attributions down to per-route and model variant. Customer asked about VPC/private deployment, SOC 2, and expected accuracy tradeoffs when using quantized models. Agreed next steps: grant sandbox, send SOC2/security pack, run a 1-week pilot with HelioWorks sample traffic.
action_items: Marcus Li; prepare sandbox with HelioWorks sample config and demo dataset; 2026-09-03
Sofia Patel; send pricing tiers + pilot contract template; 2026-09-01
Dana Ortiz; share anonymized billing export and sample request traces; 2026-09-02
next_steps: Share Dashboard Studio sandbox invite and a short how-to note
Send SOC2 summary, security pack, and KMS/HSM integration notes
Schedule pilot kickoff (1-week traffic run) week of Sep 6
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Dana (HelioWorks), Evan (HelioWorks), Priya (HelioWorks finance)
Link shared: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/helioworks-demo (screen share)

Summary (auto): Quick product walkthrough of Dashboard Studio focusing on mapping traffic to cost, per-route lenses, and pilot scoping.

00:00 Sofia: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, i'm sofia from redwood inference, i'll run the intro and then marcus will jump into the Dashboard Studio demo.
00:12 Dana: hi thanks, dana here, curious to see how you map traffic down to model variants and what the cost picture looks like.
00:18 Marcus: cool, we'll show the per-path lenses, the cost decomposition view and then a sandbox where you can upload a billing export and sample traces, gives you per-route, per-model and per-deployment cost.
00:29 Evan: quick question upfront, our stack is mostly GKE with private subnets, we do use a mix of hosted and on-prem models, is that supported?
00:36 Marcus: yep, Dashboard Studio sits on top of the same runtime so we can route by policy — hosted for burst, dedicated/pinned for steady traffic, and private deploys via a VPC peering flow. there are a few config bits, we can share a runbook.
00:52 Priya: from finance perspective we need to see chargeback by team and by route and also a forecast for month-end, can the dashboard do that?
01:01 Sofia: yes forecasting is a built-in lens, you can group by route, model, tag; we also export CSVs for accounting.
01:10 Marcus: ok jumping into the screen — opening Dashboard Studio, top-left is the global usage heatmap, you can filter by timeframe, route, model family. i'll open the HelioWorks sample dataset.
01:28 Marcus: so here you see traffic volume, 99th latency and cost per token. note the spike at 10:15 in the sample — that's shown in a timeline and we can link that to the route and downstream model variant.
01:45 Dana: hm that spike, is that because of a batching change or a model switch?
01:52 Marcus: good call — we have an event overlay, it shows an autoscaling event followed by a quantize rollout. sometimes quantization changes can cause cost to drop but inference quality might drift, we also surface quality regressions.
02:07 Evan: can you show me the per-route breakdown, like for our "assist-compose" route where we do long context?
02:15 Marcus: sure filter to assist-compose — now look right side: per-model cost slice, token counts, average streaming time. you can expand the model variant table to see pinned vs fallback runs.
02:32 Marcus: the cost decomposition does a token math: compute, memory, infra amortization, and route attribution. it's not perfect but we've seen it be within 8-12% of internal billings for most customers.
02:47 Priya: can we map to our GL codes? we need the chargeback to match our chart of accounts.
02:54 Sofia: yes you can add custom tags, map routes to GL codes and export mappings. we'll include a template.
03:05 Dana: security question — where do traces live? we have strict retention and keys need to remain in our KMS.
03:12 Marcus: for private deployments traces and KV caches remain inside your VPC, and we support customer managed keys, our control plane receives only metadata if you choose that mode. for hosted, we offer configurable retention and encryption at rest.
03:28 Dana: and SOC 2?
03:30 Sofia: we're SOC 2 Type II — i'll send the compliance pack after the call.
03:35 Evan: when you say "fallback to smaller model" what are the rules? we worry about hallucination risks.
03:41 Marcus: routing policies can be latency-first or cost-first, and fallbacks are tested against a small eval set you provide to ensure quality bounds. if an eval shows regressions we won't recommend that fallback.
03:54 Evan: ok, how disruptive is a pilot — like data, instrumentation?
04:00 Sofia: low disruption — pilot usually runs with a traffic mirror for one week where we take a sample of your requests (anonymized) and run them through the sandbox to produce the usage and cost map. we need a billing export and about 100k sample requests to get a representative view.
04:18 Dana: we can do that, we just need to ensure PII is stripped.
04:23 Marcus: yes we support anonymization hooks and you can run the mirror in your VPC so raw payloads never leave your network if you want.
04:35 Marcus: back to the demo — here's the per-route anomaly detector, it highlights routes with sudden token cost changes and links to traces and to prompts that are outliers.
04:49 Evan: nice, does it alert into slack or our pager?
04:52 Marcus: yes webhooks and slack integration, you can also set severity and who owns the alert.
05:00 Priya: show me the pricing impact — like if we turn on continuous batching, what's the delta?
05:06 Marcus: toggling batching in the model profile simulates cost and latency changes. in the sample it drops token compute cost by ~28% but 95th latency goes up 40ms. the dashboard shows the unit economics.
05:25 Dana: what about quantized models — does quality change show up?
05:29 Marcus: we surface eval diffs and examples. For some tasks quantization is fine, for others like clinical summarization it can regress. you'd run evals on your prompt set; Optimize suggests which layers to quantize and where to keep FP16.
05:46 Evan: do you have an API for pulling per-route cost programmatically?
05:50 Sofia: yes the Redwood API has endpoints for per-route telemetry and cost reports, we can provide sample SDK calls.
05:58 Marcus: now i'm going to open the traffic-to-cost exploder — it breaks down one day of traffic into a Sankey: user cohort -> route -> model variant -> infra bucket. you can click each node and see the raw queries and token histograms.
06:21 Dana: can we combine with our A/B experiment tags?
06:24 Marcus: absolutely — tags from your request headers map into the route dimensions.
06:31 Priya: pricing question — for a pilot what units do you bill? tokens or seat?
06:36 Sofia: pilot is usage-based with a capped monthly commit for the trial — tokens + infra surcharge for dedicated runs if you opt into those. we'll send a sample pilot SOW.
06:47 Evan: latency SLOs for hosted vs dedicated?
06:51 Marcus: hosted is best-effort with SLAs on higher tiers, dedicated gives you pinned capacity and SLO guarantees. for low-variance workloads we recommend dedicated.
06:59 Dana: one more on deployment — we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, can Redwood stream those?
07:05 Marcus: yes we have audit log exports to S3/GCS and streaming webhooks to SIEMs; for private it can be delivered directly inside your VPC.
07:16 Sofia: quick note, i'll drop a link to the SOC2 pack and the pilot pricing spreadsheet into the calendar invite.
07:23 Dana: perfect.
07:26 Marcus: ok wrapping up, final demo snippet — opening anomaly drilldown, showing example prompt diff where cost ramped because of longer context due to a broken client-side prompt.
07:41 Evan: ouch, we had that once. cool — that would help ops.
07:45 Sofia: Action items recap: marcus to prepare sandbox and demo dataset, sofia to send pricing and security docs, dana to share billing export. schedule pilot kickoff for week of Sep 6.
07:59 Priya: timeline approved on our end pending legal review.
08:04 Dana: thanks everyone, appreciated the demo.
08:07 Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up by Friday with invites and docs.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (speaker overlap at 04:35-04:52), product names sometimes transcribed as "Dashboard Studio" vs "Studio Dashboard". References: shared deck (link in calendar), pilot pricing spreadsheet (will be attached).
